variants.title: AM.III.F.S11 – Replace a Wire Bundle Lacing
variants.variant: AM.III.F.S11 – Replace a Wire Bundle Lacing

you_need_to.text: Be currently enrolled in or have completed Block 06: Communications & Navigation Systems, Aircraft & Electrical Systems.
Review pages 9-86 to 9-89 from chapter 9 in the FAA-H-8083-31B.
Ask the AI Assistant about the use of different knots when securing wire bundles.

safety.text: Careful clipping of lacing cord ends must be done to avoid accidental wire damage.
Knots that are not secured with a locking knot may unravel from aircraft vibrations.

steps.text: Cut the required length of lacing cord2.
steps.text_clean: Cut the required length of lacing cord.

notes.text: Gather the wires to be bundled together. Must be 1” in diameter or less. Pull the slack out of the wires and use a tape measure to identify the distance.
Multiply the distance by 2. Cut that length of lacing cord (e.g., measured distance is 4’. Cut 8’ of lacing cord to use).

sections.section: Tie a Starting Knot Using the Single Cord-Lacing Method

steps.text: Secure with a double-looped overhand knot4.
steps.text_clean: Secure with a double-looped overhand knot.

notes.text: Start the lacing at a clear section of the bundle, free of obstacles.
Pass about 8” of cord behind the bundle. Pull the cord from both sides, making a V around the bundle.

Pass the 8” strand all the way around the bundle once. Cross the short strand over the long strand and under the loop made. Tightly cinch the hitch to the bundle. Keep tension on the ends to avoid the knot from slipping.
Cross the short cord over the long cord four times back towards the clove hitch. Pull both ends until taut. Clip excess tail cord off.

sections.section: Tie a Hitch Along the Bundle

steps.text: Pull the run of the lacing cord to the next hitch.
steps.text_clean: Pull the run of the lacing cord to the next hitch.

steps.text: Repeat for as many hitches needed.
steps.text_clean: Repeat for as many hitches needed.

notes.text: Maintain equal distance between each hitch for uniformity and security. An approximate 6” gap provides adequate support. Grasp the bundle by wrapping your fingers around it about 1” away from the previous knot. Start the hitch 1” from the end of your hand by pulling the cord taut to that spot.

Pass the cord around the bundle. Align the hitch to the previous knot. Cross the end of the cord over and then under the loop made by the cord running down the bundle. Pull the end all the way through until the hitch is tight.

sections.section: Tie a Finishing Knnot on a Bundle

steps.text: Secure with a double-looped overhand knot4.
steps.text_clean: Secure with a double-looped overhand knot.

notes.text: Keep the spacing of the hitches if possible. If not, provide adequate space to perform the finishing knot.
Hold constant tension on the previous hitch. Grab the cord and bundle firmly in one hand, letting the end of the cord hang freely.

Loosely loop the end of the cord around the bundle twice. Cross the end of the cord over the run of cord from the previous hitch. Feed the end of the cord under the loop made going towards the previous hitch. Pull the slack out of the cord until tight.
Slip the end of the cord over-and-under the taut lacing toward the finishing knot four times. Pull tension on the cord past the finishing knot.
Look along the cord lacing looking for misaligned knots, looseness, and long strands.
